newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps -Jet rebounds on short covering.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps -Jet rebounds on short covering.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel swaps firmed late afternoon Wednesday on short covering and market talks of tight prompt supplies, traders said.
"Jet recovered today because of short covering by some players and talks of limited prompt supplies," one trader said.
The February jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade firmed to $3.20/$3.40 per barrel from Tuesday's $2.90/$3.10, brokers said.
They said there were talks that the market traded today at around the $3.20 per barrel level but could not confirm any deals.
March swaps edged up slightly and was last quoted at $1.90/$2.30 per barrel, against $1.80/$2.20 on Tuesday.
Traders said firmer prices were also due to a supply squeeze after several refiners in Singapore reduced their crude runs on poor margins.
Cuts in Singapore crude runs and peak seasonal demand from Indonesia for the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan has led to a price spurt, they said.
Indonesia bought a 120,000-barrel cargo from a European major last week at 53 cents premium to spot Singapore quotes on a free-on-board basis--about 20 cents more than the last deal.
Gas oil swaps were unchanged with trading range-bound in the absence of any fresh indicators.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted at $25.80/$25.80 per barrel in quiet trading with March was indicated at $26.10/$26.30.
Front month Singapore fuel oil swaps were steady in the afternoon after putting on $1.00 per tonne earlier due to the firmer crude prices.
February swaps was last quoted at $99.00/$100.00 per tonne, up from Tuesday's $98.00/$99.50, brokers said.
The market traded down to a low of $98.00 a tonne on Tuesday from a day's high of $100.00 in very active trading.
February Brent crude closed up 20 cents to $22.25 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange on Tuesday.
Naphtha was quoted higher in line with the 20-cent hike to crude values with February called at $23.40/$23.70 per barrel, one broker said.
